research_question: Can training-only depth improve RGB episode BCS through ordinal transfer beyond standard distillation and acquisition-condition controls?
backbone: ImageNet ResNet18; stages stem through layer3 frozen; layer4 and prediction head trained
pool: Within-episode decoded-RGB representatives; same cohort for every variant
aggregation: Mean of frame features, excluding padding completely
head: Linear(512 per modality,128), ReLU, Dropout(0.3), Linear(128,5)
class_weight: Inverse square root of training episode counts; mean normalised to one
selection: Lowest unweighted validation MAE using expected BCS, tie broken by validation cross entropy; test never used for selection
teacher: Depth-only trained on exactly the same training groups; checkpoint selected on validation only
boundary_weight: max(0, (q_RGB-y_binary)^2-(q_Depth-y_binary)^2), computed with softened teacher probabilities on deterministic training episodes; weights detached, multiplied by the ordinal CDF squared loss, no sample deletion
weight_normalisation: Divide by the global mean positive weight over training boundary targets; clamp weights to [0,4]; zero if no positive training weight
shuffle_control: Permute training episode depth-teacher probability vectors within native-width-majority strata, requiring a different animal group where possible; fixed seed, mapping logged, no test inputs used
primary_endpoint: Episode expected-score MAE on the original 1-9 scale (represented classes 2-6)
uncertainty: Animal-group cluster paired bootstrap of seed-averaged out-of-fold episode absolute errors; seeds and folds are not independent animal replicates
hypothesis: Benefit-weighted ordinal transfer reduces expected-score MAE versus RGB_ordinal and conventional depth KD; directional empirical hypothesis, not a guaranteed result
negative_results: Retain and report all prespecified variants, seeds and folds; no variant removal based on outer test results
data_reuse: Existing public dataset and outer groups reused from the prior Animals study; preprocessing, training protocol and deployment question differ
scope: Single-source dataset evaluation; no independent farm, prospective deployment or physical depth reconstruction claim
